correctness.rationale: Condition on k labeled cyclic roots and their permutation. The directed matrix-tree determinant det(nI_m-J_m)=k n^(m-1) counts rooted directed forests, m=n-k. For r marked nonroot terminals, removing them and attaching each to one of n-r remaining vertices gives probability (1-r/n)^(m-1), hence exact factorial moments and binomial-inversion PMF equal to m specified boxes avoided by m-1 uniform draws. The k=n boundary has Z=0. Conditional mean g_m=m(1-1/n)^(m-1) is strictly increasing m; since all k occur with positive mass, any strictly increasing h(C) has strictly negative covariance with Z. Conditioning on a fixed vertex being absent from the image gives C distributed as the cyclic count of a uniform mapping on n-1 other vertices, yielding Cov(C,Z)=n q_n^n(c_(n-1)-c_n). Standard Gaussian Riemann sums and Rayleigh scaling give the covariance and correlation constants. Independent brute force enumerated every function for n=2,3,4,5 (4+27+256+3125) and checked exact joint PMF and cyclic marginals; finite checks are not the unbounded proof.

value.rationale: The cyclic core controls long-term iteration, while terminal vertices measure one-step image depletion. Their exact finite joint null distribution and strict negative regression for every increasing transform link two natural but previously separately studied random-map statistics, supporting structural calibration and dependence analysis.

limitations: Uniform independent images [n]->[n] only; no stochastic dominance of full conditional laws claimed, only strictly decreasing conditional means.
Asymptotic constants require the analytic Gaussian and Rayleigh approximations, not the finite enumeration.
